newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela honours Gandhi.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela honours Gandhi.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela on Friday honoured India's independence leader Mahatma Gandhi with a posthumous award marking his peaceful campaign for racial equality in South Africa.

"Today we are righting a century-old wrong," Mandela said in a prepared speech to mark the award of the Freedom of the City of Pietermaritzburg on Gandhi, which was accepted by Indian High Commissioner Gopal Krishna Gandhi on behalf of his grandfather.

"It is a token of our appreciation of Mahatma Gandhi's enormous contribution to the birth of...the new South Africa. It is a token of our gratitude to the people of India who stood by us during the darkest moments in our history," Mandela added.

Gandhi's first brush with racism was at the Pietermaritzburg Station, west of the Indian Ocean port of Durban, 103 years ago when he was evicted from a first-class train compartment which was reserved for whites.
He later said his campaign of active non-violence began on that day.
Mandela, who served 27 years in jail for his opposition to apartheid, said he hoped the posthumous award to Gandhi would "in contrast to that shameful day...proclaim a message of dignity restored".
Gopal Krishna Gandhi said in a speech his self-sacrificing grandfather would not have wanted the award in order to remind the world of discrimination he had endured.

"But he would accept this honour because it would enable us to remember that the larger world remains discriminatory, remains unequal...Through this gesture South Africa is reminding the world once again that racism belongs now to the past."
Meanwhile, Mandela's office said on Thursday that India's Prime Minister, Inder Kumar Gujral, had accepted an invitation to pay a state visit later this year. No official date has been set.
Indo-South African trade touched $220 million in 1994/95 (April-March) and reached $260 million in the first half of 1995/96.
During his third visit to New Delhi, Mandela said last month he expected annual bilateral trade with India to pass $2 billion in the next three years.
